newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities steady to higher.

text.p: Singapore government securities were steady to higher on Wednesday in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said.

"The interbank rate fell slightly today but there was little impact on the market. Treasury bill yields were slightly higher but bond prices were steady to slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.95/2.90 percent compared with Tuesday's yield of 2.85/2.80 percent and one-year at a yield of 2.73/2.68 percent against 2.72/2.67 percent.
Among bonds, April 1999 was unchanged from Tuesday's close of S$98.53/98.58.
May 2002 ended at S$99.35/99.40 versus Tuesday's close of S$99.33/99.38 and June 2003 at S$94.38/94.43 against S$94.35/94.40.
The overnight interbank offered rate fell to 2-11/16 2-9/16 percent from Tuesday's 3-3/8 3-1/4 percent.
